item.title: Romania joins global race in semiconductor technology with new innovation cluster
item.description: The initiative aims to promote the production of semiconductor components, develop research and development infrastructure, and strengthen cooperation between the industrial and academic sectors. As part of the project, high-tech laboratories will be established, and specialized professionals will be trained to meet the growing needs of the semiconductor industry.

item.title: Saudi Aramco achieves significant progress in its gas production plan
item.description: Saudi Aramco has announced the achievement of significant progress in its plan to expand gas production, with the start of production at the Jafurah field, the largest unconventional gas field in the Middle East, and the commencement of operational activities at the Tanajib Gas Plant, one of the largest gas plants in the world, AzerNEWS reports, citing Arab News.

item.title: Lebanon's prime minister warns against dragging country into 'adventures'
item.description: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam on Saturday said he would not accept anyone dragging "the country into adventures that threaten its security and unity", in an indirect message to the Iran-backed Lebanese armed group Hezbollah, AzerNEWS reports, citing Tribune.

item.title: N. Korea releases rare photo of leader's daughter firing rifle
item.description: North Korea on Saturday released a rare solo photo of leader Kim Jong-un's daughter Ju-ae taking aim at a target with a sniper rifle, after she took center stage with her father at a key military parade, AzerNEWS reports, citing Yonhap.

item.title: Germany considers expanding domestic gas production amid energy debate
item.description: As Germany prepares to implement the planned “Building Modernization” law, discussions over the country’s gas supply and alternative energy sources have intensified.

item.title: Baku’s oil backbone holds firm as global markets shift
item.description: In recent months, global energy markets have once again reminded us of their volatility. Oil prices, buffeted by geopolitical tensions and shifting trade dynamics, remain at the center of economic debates worldwide. For energy-exporting nations, these fluctuations represent strategic challenges that can reshape fiscal stability and long-term development. As for Azerbaijan, a country whose economy is deeply intertwined with oil and gas revenues, stands as a vivid example of this reality.

item.title: China's carbon dioxide emissions per 10,000 yuan of GDP down 5 pct in 2025
item.description: China's carbon dioxide emissions per 10,000 yuan (1,445 U.S. dollars) of GDP fell 5 percent year on year in 2025, as the country made notable progress in energy conservation and carbon reduction, official data showed on Saturday, AzerNEWS reports, citing Xinhua.

item.title: Iran to form temporary leadership council today, as death of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei confirmed
item.description: Israel has carried out a preemptive strike against Iran, AzerNEWS reports, citing Israeli media outlets.

item.title: Middle East tensions disrupt over 1,800 flights as major airlines suspend routes
item.description: Escalating processes in the Middle East have significantly disrupted global air travel, affecting hundreds of flights from various regions around the world.

item.title: Israel seeking to partition Iran, says national security chief
item.description: Ali Larijani, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, has accused Israel of “seeking to partition” the country following its joint attack with the US, AzerNEWS reports.
